title: A connector auth key drained on save (#28640 ②B) still sits in cleartext at rest in sys_metadata_history snapshots
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmSduNGC2SZXszyrNut

Ruled: 6677709817 · letter d (c, then b) · 2026-11-06T05:28Z
Ruling-ref: 6677709817

Filing gate: ① an out-of-scope finding (class b, carrier: the seat) the #28640 dev noted on PR #29456 (os-dev-report 6581427705) and the seat's contract review confirmed (record 6581889597). ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

## What was measured

PR #29456 (ruling ②B, 6566912252) makes a save of a connector's served form drop a leftover undeclared `auth` key (for example a legacy `auth.token`) from the live `sys_metadata` row, and tells the author with a `withheld-key-dropped` advisory. The `sys_metadata_history` snapshots written before that save keep the pre-drain body, value included.

A read of a history row is served through the stored-row seam (`redactStoredMetadataRow(s)` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts`), which withholds the key, so there is no cleartext exit through the API. The value is cleartext only at rest, in history rows, for as long as history is retained.

## Wanted

The maintainer's call on whether at-rest history must be scrubbed too: (a) leave it, documented (history is served redacted; retention bounds it); (b) a one-time scrub of undeclared `auth` keys from connector history snapshots, as a migration step; or (c) withhold at write time for future history rows only. Any option that rewrites stored history is a data change and goes to the maintainer first.

Reader who acts: `domain:server` (metadata history writer) with the `domain:spec` redaction owner, after triage.

Related: #28640 / PR #29456, ruling 6566912252.
